title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' manuscript. Π_{0,3} is π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}), free on the loops l_0, l_1, l_∞ with one product relation. Π_{0,3}·{1,τ} is its extension by complex conjugation. 𝔖_{0,3} is the group generated by Π_{0,3}, the anharmonic S_3 symmetries and conjugation, acting on the universal cover of U_{0,3} = M_{0,4}.

Top of page. This finishes the previous page's discussion of fixed points. The D_3 = 𝔖'_3 lift fixing −j̄ has a second Π_{0,3}-conjugacy class, attached to −j. It is obtained by conjugating by any of the reflections τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞, since complex conjugation swaps j and j̄.

Section III: relation with the triangulated non-oriented cartographic group.
- He defines Π'_{0,3} as the orbifold fundamental group of P^1 with a puncture at 0 (weight 0, i.e. infinite order), an order-2 point at 1 and an order-3 point at ∞.
- Equivalently, Π'_{0,3} = Π_{0,3}/⟨⟨l_1^2, l_∞^3⟩⟩ ≅ Z/2 * Z/3 ≅ PSL(2,Z). The marginal 'Sl(2,Z)' should be read projectively.
- The non-oriented version, the tilde group (the quotient of Π_{0,3}·{1,τ}), has three involutive generators σ_0, σ_1, σ_2. Here σ_i changes the i-th component of a flag/biarc: σ_0 is the tangential orientation change, σ_2 the transversal one, σ_1 the passage to the adjacent biarc.
- Relations (25): σ_i^2 = 1, (σ_2σ_0)^2 = 1, (σ_1σ_0)^3 = 1. This is Grothendieck's cartographic group C_2 plus the triangulation condition ρ_f^3 = 1. As a reflection group it is the extended (2,3,∞) triangle group ≅ PGL(2,Z).
- Oriented index-2 subgroup: generated by ρ_f = σ_1σ_0, ρ_s = σ_2σ_1, σ = σ_0σ_2. By Reidemeister–Schreier its relations are (26): ρ_f σ ρ_s = 1, σ^2 = ρ_f^3 = 1.
- Hence (27): Π_{0,3} → Π'_{0,3} with l_0 ↦ ρ_s, l_1 ↦ σ, l_∞ ↦ ρ_f, which is surjective with kernel normally generated by l_1^2, l_∞^3.
- The page breaks off saying this homomorphism extends to the non-oriented groups. The next page does this, sending τ_i ↦ σ'_i, and then identifies the tilde group with 𝔖_{0,3} (≅ PGL(2,Z)) and Π'_{0,3} with 𝔖^+_{0,3} (≅ PSL(2,Z) = ⟨σ_∞, ρ | σ_∞^2 = ρ^3 = 1⟩).

Purpose: to interpret the modular/Teichmüller symmetry group of M_{0,4} as the cartographic group of triangulated maps (dessins). This links the 'équation des lacets' set-up to the dessins d'enfants dictionary of the Esquisse.
errors: Marginal 'Sl(2,Z)': the group Π'_{0,3} = Z/2*Z/3 is PSL(2,Z), and its non-oriented extension is PGL(2,Z), not SL(2,Z). This is a standard abuse of notation, not a mathematical error.
No substantive errors. Relations (25), the index-2 subgroup generators and the presentation (26) check out by Reidemeister–Schreier: ρ_fσρ_s = σ_1σ_0σ_0σ_2σ_2σ_1 = 1.

ideas.what: Cartographic group with involutions σ_0, σ_1, σ_2 (σ_i^2 = 1, (σ_0σ_2)^2 = 1) and its oriented index-2 subgroup generated by ρ_s, ρ_f, σ with ρ_fσρ_s = 1, σ^2 = 1
ideas.modern_name: Cartographic group C_2 / C_2^+ (flag/monodromy group of maps)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); developed by Malgoire–Voisin, Jones–Singerman

ideas.what: Imposing ρ_f^3 = 1 (triangulated maps) gives Z/2*Z/3 ≅ PSL(2,Z), and the non-oriented version is the extended (2,3,∞) triangle group ≅ PGL(2,Z)
ideas.modern_name: Triangulated maps ↔ finite-index subgroups of PSL(2,Z); extended modular group as a Coxeter-type triangle group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Fricke); map interpretation by Grothendieck (Esquisse) and Jones–Singerman (1978)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (remark on triangulated maps and SL(2,Z))

ideas.what: Π'_{0,3} as the orbifold π_1 of P^1 with signature (∞,2,3), i.e. the quotient of π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) by l_1^2, l_∞^3
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold fundamental group of the modular curve X(1) with its elliptic points

ideas.what: Second conjugacy class of the lifted D_3-stabiliser (the fixed point −j) obtained by conjugating by any of the reflections τ_i
ideas.modern_name: Conjugacy classes of finite subgroups ↔ fixed points (orbifold points of M_{0,4} under S_3 ⋊ conjugation)

deep.surprise_reason: The page re-derives standard facts: the triangulated cartographic group is PSL(2,Z), and its non-oriented version is PGL(2,Z) as the (2,3,∞) reflection group. Grothendieck already stated these in the Esquisse, and they are classical. The only personal touch is setting this up to identify the symmetry group of M_{0,4} with the cartographic group, which is also well known (Γ(2) ⊂ PSL(2,Z)).
transcription_corrections: 't[?]-gentilles' should read 'tangentielle': σ_0 and σ_2 are resp. the tangential resp. transversal change of orientation.
The phrase '[-du rang i-] du repère' is better read as: σ_i changes the component of rank i of the repère (flag), hence acts within a biarc.
Right margin of the Π' formula reads roughly '≃ Sl(2,Z)' (meaning PSL(2,Z)), not 'avec Sl(2,Z)'.
The left marginal note concerns renaming σ_2 as σ_∞ so the generators correspond to (τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞).
